questions.question: What are the two basic approaches of structural analysis? Explain the principle of superposition and its limitations with illustrative examples.
Explain the criteria for static determinacy, indeterminacy and stability of planar and spatial structures with neat sketches and examples.
Derive an expression for strain energy stored in a straight beam due to bending moment, axial force and shear force.

A 50 kg load drops by 10 cm on a simply supported beam of 4 m span having width 30 mm and depth 150 mm. E = 200 GPa. Use strain energy method to determine the maximum dynamic deflection and maximum bending stress induced in the beam.
State and prove the principle of virtual work (unit load method) for determining deflections in trusses and beams.

For a pin-jointed plane truss, calculate the vertical and horizontal deflection at a loaded joint due to: (i) external joint loads, (ii) a temperature change of 20°C in bottom chord members, and (iii) a fabrication lack of fit where one diagonal member is 3 mm too long. Take A = 800 mm^2, E = 200 GPa, and α = 1.2 × 10^-5 /°C.
State and prove Mohr's Moment-Area theorems. Determine the slope and deflection at the center and overhanging tip of a simply supported overhanging beam using moment-area method.

Explain the conjugate beam method and its relationships with the real beam. Determine the slope and deflection at the free end and intermediate points of a stepped cantilever beam using the conjugate beam method.

Define Influence Line Diagram (ILD) and describe its practical importance in the design of bridges and moving load structures. Determine the criteria for absolute maximum bending moment in a simply supported girder.

A train of wheel loads crosses a simply supported girder of span 20 m from left to right. Determine: (i) the maximum bending moment and shear force at a section 8 m from the left support, and (ii) the absolute maximum bending moment developed in the girder.

Draw influence line diagrams for forces in members U1U2, U2L2, and L2L3 of a through-type Pratt truss. Determine the maximum forces in these members when a uniformly distributed load of intensity 20 kN/m and length 6 m passes through the bottom chord.

A three-hinged parabolic arch of span 40 m and central rise 8 m carries a moving uniformly distributed load of 30 kN/m of length 15 m. With the help of influence lines, calculate the maximum positive and negative bending moments, radial shear and normal thrust at a section 10 m from the left support.

Show that the bending moment at any section of a three-hinged parabolic arch subjected to uniformly distributed load over its entire span is zero everywhere. Deduce the expression for normal thrust and radial shear under this condition.

A suspension cable of 80 m span and 8 m dip is stiffened by a three-hinged girder. It carries a dead load of 10 kN/m. Determine maximum tension in the cable and maximum bending moment at a section 20 m from the left support in the girder when a moving UDL of intensity 15 kN/m longer than the span passes through the girder. Also draw BMD and SFD for the girder.

A cable is suspended between two supports at different levels with span of 50 m. The left support is 3 m below the right support and the lowest point of the cable is 5 m below the lower support. The cable carries a UDL of 15 kN/m horizontally across the entire span. Calculate the length of the cable, the horizontal thrust, and the maximum tension in the cable.
Explain the tension coefficient method for the analysis of space trusses. State the equations of equilibrium and boundary conditions used in the analysis of space frames.

Analyze a tripod space truss supported on spherical hinges at ground level and loaded by a combined vertical and horizontal force at the top apex joint. Determine the tension or compression in all members using tension coefficient method.

questions.text: State Castigliano's First and Second Theorems. Apply Castigliano's Theorem to find the vertical and horizontal deflection at the free end of a curved quarter-circular cantilever beam or portal frame.
questions.solutionOutline: Castigliano Theorem 1: partial derivative of strain energy with respect to displacement equals corresponding applied force: dU/ddelta_i = P_i. Castigliano Theorem 2: partial derivative of complementary strain energy (or strain energy for linearly elastic material) with respect to force equals displacement: dU/dP_i = delta_i. For curved quarter-circular cantilever with vertical end load P: M(theta) = P R sin(theta); strain energy U = integral_0^{pi/2} [P^2 R^2 sin^2(theta) / (2EI)] R dtheta => delta_v = dU/dP = (pi P R^3) / (4EI).

questions.text: Explain the Principle of Virtual Work (Unit Load Method) for trusses: $\Delta = \sum \frac{n N L}{A E}$. Determine the vertical deflection of a loaded lower chord joint of a statically determinate plane pin-jointed truss.
questions.solutionOutline: Real system has actual loads producing internal member axial forces N. Virtual system applies dummy unit load 1.0 at desired joint in desired deflection direction, producing internal member virtual forces n. Work-energy balance: 1.0 * Delta = sum n * Delta L = sum (n N L) / (A E). Tabulate members, length L, area A, real force N, virtual force n, and calculate sum (n N L / A E).

questions.text: Use the Unit Load Method (Dummy Unit Load method) to determine the vertical deflection and slope at the mid-span of a simply supported beam with non-prismatic variable flexural rigidity $E I$.
questions.solutionOutline: For beams, virtual work equation is 1.0 * Delta = integral_0^L [m(x) M(x) / (E I)] dx, where M(x) is real bending moment due to applied loads, and m(x) is virtual bending moment due to dummy unit load at midspan. For slope theta, apply dummy unit moment 1.0 at midspan: 1.0 * theta = integral_0^L [m_theta(x) M(x) / (EI)] dx. Integrate piecewise across sections of varying flexural rigidity EI.

questions.text: Explain Strain Energy stored due to axial force, bending moment ($U = \int \frac{M^2 dx}{2EI}$), shear force, and torsion. State and prove Betti's Law and Maxwell's Reciprocal Deflection Theorem.
questions.solutionOutline: Axial: U = integral N^2 dx / (2AE). Bending: U = integral M^2 dx / (2EI). Torsion: U = integral T^2 dx / (2GJ). Betti law: in any linearly elastic structure, virtual work done by system of forces P1 acting through displacements caused by system of forces P2 equals work done by P2 acting through displacements caused by P1: sum P1_i * delta_{2i} = sum P2_j * delta_{1j}. Maxwell reciprocal theorem (special case for unit loads): deflection at point j due to unit load at i equals deflection at i due to unit load at j: delta_ji = delta_ij.

questions.text: Construct Influence Line Diagrams (ILD) for support reactions, shear force, and bending moment at a given section $C$ of a simply supported beam. Calculate the maximum shear force and bending moment caused by a moving train of concentrated wheel loads.
questions.solutionOutline: ILD represents variation of a structural response (reaction, shear, moment) at fixed section as unit load traverses across span. ILD for R_A is triangle from 1 at A to 0 at B. ILD for shear at C drops by 1.0 from x/L to -(L-x)/L. ILD for BM at C is triangle peaking at x(L-x)/L. For train of moving loads, maximum moment occurs under a load when that load divides beam in same ratio as section C divides span (average load on left = average load on right).

questions.text: Construct Influence Line Diagrams for axial forces in the top chord, bottom chord, and vertical/diagonal web members of a Pratt or Warren truss under a rolling unit load on the bottom deck.
questions.solutionOutline: Pass imaginary vertical cut through panel containing target member. Top/bottom chord forces found by method of sections: taking moment about opposing joint yields chord force proportional to bending moment at that joint (triangular ILD). Web diagonal force found by vertical shear equilibrium: diagonal force F_diag = V_panel / sin(theta). ILD for diagonal mirrors panel shear, with linear transition between panel panel-point joints.

questions.text: Analyze a Three-Hinged Parabolic Arch with hinges at both springings and crown. Derive the expression for horizontal thrust $H = \frac{w L^2}{8 h}$ under a uniformly distributed load $w$ over the entire span, and prove that the resultant bending moment is identically zero everywhere.
questions.solutionOutline: Arch profile y = 4h x(L - x) / L^2. Vertical reactions V_A = V_B = w L / 2. Take moment about crown hinge C: sum M_c = 0 => V_A (L/2) - w (L/2)^2 / 2 - H * h = 0 => H = w L^2 / (8 h). At any section x: beam moment M_0(x) = (w L x / 2) - (w x^2 / 2) = w x (L - x) / 2. Arch bending moment M(x) = M_0(x) - H * y = w x (L - x) / 2 - [w L^2 / (8h)] * [4h x (L - x) / L^2] = 0 identically for all x, proving parabolic arch is funicular shape for UDL.

questions.text: Analyze a Three-Hinged Circular Arch carrying concentrated point loads. Calculate the normal thrust ($N$) and radial shear ($Q$) at a section defined by angular coordinate $\theta$ from the support.
questions.solutionOutline: Determine horizontal thrust H and vertical reactions V_A, V_B. At section x, vertical shear is V_x = V_A - sum W_left, and horizontal force is H. The tangent to arch axis makes angle theta with horizontal. Resolve forces along tangent and normal: Normal thrust N = H cos(theta) + V_x sin(theta); Radial shear Q = V_x cos(theta) - H sin(theta). Resultant axial compression reduces tensile flexural cracking.

questions.text: Construct Influence Line Diagrams for horizontal thrust $H$, bending moment, normal thrust, and radial shear at a given section of a Three-Hinged Parabolic Arch.
questions.solutionOutline: ILD for H: unit load at distance z from left support. For z <= L/2, taking moment about crown gives H = z / (2h); for z > L/2, H = (L - z) / (2h). Peak value of H is L / (4h) when unit load is at crown hinge. ILD for bending moment at section x is difference between beam moment ILD and arch thrust relief H * y: ILD(M_x) = ILD(M_0) - y * ILD(H), creating positive and negative lobes.

questions.text: Derive the cable profile equation for a flexible suspension cable carrying a uniformly distributed load $w$ per horizontal meter. Derive cable tension $T = \sqrt{H^2 + V^2}$, maximum tension at the support, and total cable length $S = L + \frac{8h^2}{3L}$.
questions.solutionOutline: Flexible cable carries only axial tension. Differential equation of cable: d^2y/dx^2 = w / H. Integrating with y(0)=0 and dy/dx|_{x=L/2} = 0 yields parabolic profile y = 4h x(L - x) / L^2. Horizontal tension H is constant throughout. Vertical reaction V = w L / 2. Maximum tension occurs at highest support: T_max = sqrt(H^2 + V^2) = H sqrt(1 + (4h/L)^2). Arc length S = integral sqrt(1 + (dy/dx)^2) dx approx L + 8 h^2 / (3 L) using binomial expansion.

questions.text: Analyze a Suspension Bridge with a Three-Hinged Stiffening Girder. Calculate the cable tension, uniform upward hanger tension, and draw bending moment and shear force diagrams for the stiffening girder under rolling point loads.
questions.solutionOutline: Stiffening girder distributes concentrated live loads uniformly to suspension cable via vertical hangers. Upward hanger load per unit length is w_e = 8 H h / L^2. Girder behaves as simply supported beam subjected to external live loads acting downwards and uniform hanger pull w_e acting upwards. Moment in girder M_g(x) = M_beam(x) - H * y(x). Since girder has crown hinge, moment at crown is zero, allowing determination of H.

questions.text: Analyze a Statically Determinate Simple Space Truss using the Method of Tension Coefficients. Determine the member forces for a tripod or transmission tower subjected to horizontal and vertical joint loads.
questions.solutionOutline: Tension coefficient t_AB = T_AB / L_AB. Equilibrium equations for joint A in 3D: sum F_x = sum t_AB (x_B - x_A) + P_x = 0; sum F_y = sum t_AB (y_B - y_A) + P_y = 0; sum F_z = sum t_AB (z_B - z_A) + P_z = 0. Yields system of 3 linear algebraic equations per joint without resolving trigonometric direction cosines. Member axial force T_AB = t_AB * L_AB (positive tension, negative compression).

questions.text: Differentiate between Static Indeterminacy ($D_s$) and Kinematic Indeterminacy ($D_k$). Formulate degree of static indeterminacy ($D_s = D_{se} + D_{si}$) and kinematic indeterminacy for plane frames, space frames, and pin-jointed trusses with rigid and semi-rigid joints.
questions.solutionOutline: Static indeterminacy (D_s) is number of unknown forces exceeding available equilibrium equations: D_se = r - 3 (external), D_si = 3m - 3j (internal for closed frame loops), total D_s = 3m + r - 3j - c (c = internal releases). Kinematic indeterminacy (D_k / degrees of freedom) is number of independent joint displacements (translations and rotations): D_k = 3j - r - m_ext (unextensible members). For plane truss D_s = m + r - 2j, D_k = 2j - r.
